summary: New actual two-distinct-residue equation carrying full nonskeletal rawmass2, all positive real depths; independent masses m_i<=1 and full-dual formulas. Geometry/deeper audit/general Dirac remain open.
detailedSummary: The six-polynomial log-max is proved equal to the baseline outside two residue bidiscs and to the capped translated maximum inside each, at every analytic point. It gives an actual C weight with MA=delta_x1+delta_x2, no Gauss mass. Positive four-corner combinations and a newly proved actual cross-product identity give (2-lambda1^2-lambda2^2)g+lambda1^2 x1+lambda2^2 x2, E=-1/3-sum(lambda_i^3 c_i)/3 and FULL D=1/6+2sum(lambda_i^3 c_i)/3. All radii are positive real; no all-G uniqueness, general recognition, genuine nonalgebraization or entire-current audit is newly certified.
text:
On the supplied analytic surface K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8, X=(Gm^2)^an/<(t,2),(3,t)>, there is a new actual continuous-CLD equation with the entire raw mass two at two distinct nonskeletal residue-bidisc Gauss points. The retained geometry is compact, good, strict, smooth, separated, boundaryless and pure dimension two. Genuine nonalgebraization and coherent descent are not independently certified. The original entire minimal continuous sheaf C, local rho=|r|^2/2, theta=DD rho, cubic E, and FULL D=sup_ENTIRE_C(E(a)-int a mu) are unchanged. No incoming note is a correctness grant; the needed analytic calculus is reconstructed below.

Choose units a1,a2,b1,b2 with |a1-a2|=|b1-b2|=1; concretely a1=b1=1, a2=b2=2. On the injective ordinary chart U={|ri|<1/4}, let Di={|z1-ai|<1,|z2-bi|<1}, Pi=(ai,bi), and x_i,c the joint bidisc Gauss point of radius exp(-c), c>0. The ordinary Di are disjoint. Let q0=sum xi(1-xi)/2-1/4, xi=ri-floor(ri), g=sigma(0), and Ai=max(1,|zi|). Then rho+q0=log(A1 A2)-.5 log|z1z2|-.25 on U. At integer walls its local slopes jump positively; smooth convex maxima give q0 in the original C. Put gamma_i=max(0,-log max(|z1-ai|,|z2-bi|)) on U, zero outside U, with infinity only at Pi. Let v_i,c=-min(c,gamma_i).

THE NEW LOG-MAX IDENTITY holds at every actual analytic point, including support kernels and nonclassical points. Set u=z1-a1, v=z1-a2, p=z2-b1, q=z2-b2, R_i=exp(-c_i). Define H=log max(|uq|,|vp|,R1|v|,R1|q|,R2|u|,R2|p|). On D1, |v|=|q|=1, so H=log max(R1,|u|,|p|); on D2 it is log max(R2,|v|,|q|). Outside both discs it is log(A1 A2). Indeed max(|u|,|v|)=A1 and max(|p|,|q|)=A2. If an Ai>1 its two translated norms both equal Ai, giving the required product maximum. If both Ai=1 and |u|<1, then |v|=1 and being outside D1 forces |p|=1; the |v|<1 case is symmetric. If |u|=|v|=1, one of |p|,|q| is one. All four caps are bounded by A1 A2. Thus H=log(A1 A2)+v_1,c1+v_2,c2 globally on U.

This gives ACTUAL positivity, rather than a prescription based on values. The six slots have no common zero: common zeros of uq,vp are precisely P1,P2, and there the opposite-coordinate cap is positive. Near any point omit slots vanishing there below a nonzero slot's positive local lower bound. The remaining slots are logarithms of analytic units. Smooth convex maxima of them have positive Hessian and converge locally uniformly. Subtracting .5 log|z1z2|+.25 is smooth harmonic, so q12=q0+v_1,c1+v_2,c2 belongs locally to C. If some |zi| differs from one, both corrections vanish. In particular they vanish on the ORDINARY collar 1/8<max|ri|<1/4, so q12 glues to q0 on X. Translated coordinates are used only in the injective chart; no invariance under deck units 2,3 is assumed.

EXACT ACTUAL MEASURE: on each Di, rho+q12 is log max(R_i,|z1-ai|,|z2-bi|) plus a smooth harmonic function. CLD v2 Corollary18.6.2 states that on a boundaryless, topologically separated, equidimensional analytic space, for analytic f1,...,fd and positive real t,rj, (DD log max(t,|fj|/rj))^d equals the integration current of f^{-1}(eta_(t rj)). Here d=2, t=R_i, rj=1 and f is the translation isomorphism of an ordinary open bidisc. Its Gauss fibre is the SINGLE point x_i,ci, analytic degree one. All source hypotheses hold; no value-group condition is imposed on the positive real radii. Thus each disc carries one unit. Recursive products are positive Radon measures, and every bounded mixed mass is two: its difference from theta^2 is globally DD-exact and evaluates to zero on the global test 1. The two identified units exhaust the mass, leaving no measure anywhere else. Therefore MA(q12)=delta_x1,c1+delta_x2,c2 on ALL continuous analytic tests. Near g the caps are strictly inactive and H=log|vp|+max(0,log|uq/vp|); rank-one smooth approximations also give its square zero. The actual bounded presentation q12+2^-n decreases everywhere and has finite lower energy.

For independent masses, the following reconstruction also proves the actual cross-products. The one-well local log maximum log max(exp(-c),|z1-ai|,|z2-bi|,|(z1-ai)(z2-bi)|), minus the same harmonic term, gives q_i,c=q0+v_i,c in C with the same collar. The translated fibre gives coefficient one at x_i,c. Near g, subtract the product unit logarithm and invert both translated coordinates; the unit Gauss fibre gives coefficient one at g. Positivity and total mass give MA(q_i,c)=delta_g+delta_x_i,c. The baseline square is 2delta_g: each original-coordinate Hessian is its fixed unit Gauss curve, its own square is rank one, and the mixed fibre restricts to the other coordinate Gauss point, coefficient one. Restricting the one-well potential to either original-coordinate unit Gauss fibre gives log max(1,|z_other|), since the fixed translated coordinate has norm one. The proper fixed-fibre restriction formula gives B(q0,q_i,c)=2delta_g. Consequently, Delta_i,c=DD v_i,c satisfies theta_q0 Delta_i,c=0 and Delta_i,c^2=delta_x_i,c-delta_g. The independently proved two-well square and multilinearity now give Delta_1,c Delta_2,d=0 for EVERY positive pair of depths. This is an actual signed current identity, not an inference from disjoint negative wells.

Hence for arbitrary 0<=lambda_i<=1, q=q0+lambda1 v_1,c1+lambda2 v_2,c2 lies in C: it is the convex combination of q0,q_1,c1,q_2,c2,q12 with the four nonnegative tensor weights (1-lambda1)(1-lambda2),lambda1(1-lambda2),(1-lambda1)lambda2,lambda1lambda2. Its actual measure is (2-lambda1^2-lambda2^2)delta_g+lambda1^2 delta_x1,c1+lambda2^2 delta_x2,c2. EACH off-Gauss mass can independently reach one; their sum need not be at most one.

To check energy and the ENTIRE dual rather than a restricted maximum, here is the bounded-calculus input. For each positive closed (1,1) T, complete smooth gradients in the positive local pairing with nonnegative cutoffs. Uniform-zero functions with a strong gradient limit pair to zero against compact smooth one-form tests by closedness and finite coefficient measures; density gives closability. If L_Tf=DD(fT) is signed Radon, smooth testing and uniform/strong approximation give Q_T(f,g)=-int g L_Tf and the cutoff identity Q_T,chi(f)=int f^2 DDchi T/2-int chi f L_Tf. For uniformly convergent positive-domain f_j bounded by A on a surrounding eta with eta=1 near supp chi, epsilon=||f_j-f_k|| gives Q_T,chi(f_j-f_k)<=epsilon^2||DDchi T||TV/2+2A epsilon||chi||infinity||DDeta T||TV. Their gradients are Cauchy; diagonal smooth approximation proves the limit lies in the domain. This uniformly closed sheaf contains all smooth positive-Hessian generators, hence EVERY stage of the original minimal sheaf. Finite smooth partitions patch differences globally. Green, symmetry and cubic expansion therefore give E'(a_h)=int(b-a)MA(a_h), E''(a_h)=-2Q_theta_ah(b-a)<=0 for a_h=(1-h)a+hb. Thus E(a)-int a MA(q)<=E(q)-int q MA(q) for EVERY a in C, with equality at a=q.

Identity torus calibration, saturated lattice and analytic degree one give theta^2=2sigma_*Leb and B(q0,0)=sigma_*(delta_r1=0 dr2+dr1 delta_r2=0). Off the joint Gauss section a Laurent-polynomial strict cancellation persists on an ordinary neighbourhood and forces coordinate tropicalization into a hypersurface of dimension at most one, where the coordinate top form vanishes; on the section the wedge of the two coordinate forms supplies factor two. Since int_0^1 x(1-x)/2 dx=1/12, the three baseline moments are -1/6,-1/3,-1/2 and E(q0)=-1/3. Along q0+h(q-q0), the off-Gauss masses are h^2 lambda_i^2 and q-q0 has value -lambda_i c_i there and zero at g. Integrating the actual first variation gives E(q)=-1/3-(lambda1^3 c1+lambda2^3 c2)/3. Its target moment is -1/2-lambda1^3 c1-lambda2^3 c2, so FULL D(MA(q))=1/6+2(lambda1^3 c1+lambda2^3 c2)/3. For lambda1=lambda2=1,c1=c2=1/8, E=-5/12 and FULL D=1/3.

The entire immediate18.6.1/2 proof was read and rejudged for these isomorphisms/projections, degree one; literal prose slips about vanishing DD are excluded, using top-power rank vanishing only.6.2.4-8 smooth cutoff/density/partition statements and immediate proofs were read: local differential separation follows from15.7.1 and compact Hausdorff X is paracompact.
